references.operator: United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office treaty archive
references.document_date: Signed at Cape Town 1926-06-22; presented as Treaty Series No. 29 (1926)
references.relevant_content: Articles 1-3 resolve the Ruacana/Rua Cana waterfall identification and describe the Angola–South-West Africa line from the falls along the latitude parallel to the middle of the Okavango/Cubango, then by reference to the 1886 Lisbon treaty. Article 4 requires joint demarcation and specified beaconing/astronomical observation. Article 6 says the river middle line applies where the line follows a river and cuts an island.
references.scope_limit: Primary treaty text supports the described boundary framework. It does not itself provide a modern georeferenced coordinate polyline or the underlying completed demarcation record for these candidate polygons. The source line at issue is inland; the later 2002 maritime treaty is irrelevant.

references.id: JRC Global Surface Water v1.5 Occurrence 1984-2024
references.operator: European Commission Joint Research Centre / Google
references.document_date: Release page updated for 2024; retained official metadata identifies product creation/publication 2026-08-27. Occurrence summarizes March 1984 through December 2024.
references.retrieval_status: Both original 10E_10S and 20E_10S GeoTIFF tile byte streams retained, reassembled from size-limited custody parts, and verified against original-file SHA-256. Official occurrence ISO metadata and the v2024 Data Users Guide are retained.
references.relevant_content: The official guide defines occurrence as month-normalized frequency of surface-water detections from March 1984 through December 2024; values 1–100 represent percentage and 0 means not water. The 30 m nominal grid yields positive occurrence pixels inside all 21 unchanged candidates; candidate-level counts are in jrc-gsw-water-analysis.json.
references.use_limit: Occurrence is a long-term summary and does not date detections. The dataset describes a spatially variable residual co-registration offset at the 2022 Landsat Collection 2 transition, generally sub-pixel but at or above one 30 m pixel in some path/rows. It does not establish a specific bank, waterbody type, legal boundary, processing cause, or territorial assignment. Attribution: Source: EC JRC/Google.

references.id: League of Nations Treaty Series, vol. 129, No. 2960 (1932 publication): 1928 Kakeri Final Act and 1931 exchange of notes
references.operator: League of Nations Treaty Collection / United Nations Treaty Collection
references.document_date: Joint Final Act signed Kakeri 1928-09-23; exchange of notes 1931; published 1932
references.retrieval_status: Official full PDF retained and visually inspected, including the full joint act and beacon schedule.
references.relevant_content: The joint commission records the boundary demarcation by chords joining 47 beacons. Beacon 47 is described on a limestone ridge 240 m west of the Okavango west bank at Kakeri; its printed coordinates are 17°23′23.7″S, 18°25′06.2″E. The 1931 exchange records both governments accepting the demarcation and description as correct and recognizing the boundary indicated by the erected beacons. The act notes that clearing between beacon 28 and the Okavango remained to be completed.
references.scope_limit: Primary evidence for the historical beacon demarcation and its acceptance. It does not provide a modern datum, georeferenced current river median/banks through the candidates, subsequent joint reaffirmation, or candidate-specific territorial assignment. Beacon 47 latitude was not astronomically observed; coordinate-bounds comparisons are only coarse locator screens.

spatial_screen.method: Compare candidate latitude bounds with the approximate latitude stated for the 1926 Ruacana/Rua Cana Falls point; use only as a locator screen, not as a legal boundary test.
spatial_screen.interpretation: The candidate family lies close to and south of the approximate latitude associated with the treaty's Ruacana point, and extends east toward the Okavango/Cubango. This makes the 1926 line, the 1886 river sequence, the river's historical course, and demarcation records material. The approximate waterfall latitude and bbox are not enough to assign territory or answer authority.

beacon_47_bbox_screen.method: Raw EPSG:4326 coordinate-bound comparison only; no datum transformation, geodetic line construction, or legal test. The act states beacon 47 latitude was not astronomically observed.
beacon_47_bbox_screen.interpretation: All candidate bounding boxes fall east and south of the printed beacon-47 coordinate. Because the treaty describes the later boundary by the Okavango river sector and this screen does not reconstruct the river median or historical course, it cannot establish a boundary crossing, side, or assignment.

separate_classifications.consumed_source_geometry: Source products overlap candidate footprints by positive area; see source-geometry-comparison.json.
separate_classifications.current_physical_water_or_historic_cours: JRC GSW v1.5 provides separate 1984–2024 occurrence and 2024 seasonality observations at approximately 30 m; positive water-classified pixels occur within all 21 candidates. This supports water occurrence within the candidate footprints, not exact shoreline/current course or historical channel location. Waterbody type, floods/wetlands, collection-transition geolocation shift, and suitability for any legal line remain limits.
separate_classifications.processing_cause: Unresolved; no exact processing defect has been reproduced.
separate_classifications.international_boundary_authority: The 1926 agreement and retained 1928 joint Kakeri Final Act / 1931 exchange establish a historically demarcated beacon line accepted by both governments. The candidate family lies east and south of beacon 47 only by raw coordinate-bounds screening. The exact historical/current Okavango river-sector line through candidate footprints, later joint reaffirmation, and candidate-specific authority/assignment remain unresolved.
